QUOTE: Without the define: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(m)` → `private_m`. Members are renamed and hidden. With the define: `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(m)` → `m`. Members keep their real names. ... Inside the library and the two SSL sample programs, code can read and write struct fields directly... Everywhere else, which includes external applications... the fields are renamed and direct access fails to compile.

VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that code defining MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names, while other consumers of the public headers see the renamed `private_` members.
